subject: ventures/clearance-markdown-planner
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 115, see run record
professional: a senior retail merchandise planner / markdown-optimisation analyst; they check first that the expected-revenue-plus-salvage recursion reproduces a closed-form hold-price case, that the elasticity fit and its shrinkage reproduce by hand, that the demand level read off a log-log fit is unbiased for low-volume SKUs, and that the output carries the planning KPIs they report (sell-through, markdown dollars, margin after markdown, weeks of supply)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed four outputs with an auditor-written stdlib Python script (scratchpad indep.py), not the author's tests. (1) Hold-price baseline, units 30, price 10, 4 weeks, 6/wk, Poisson (dispersion 0), salvage 2: total demand N ~ Poisson(24), value = 10 E[min(N,30)] + 2 E[(30-N)+] = 249.6359; tool baselines[0].expectedValue 249.6348 (diff 0.001, from the +-5 sd pmf window). (2) Full markdown DP for the same case written independently by memoised recursion over (week, stock, level), levels 0-60% step 10, markdown-only: 257.6566; tool expectedValue 257.6561, path 0,0,10,20%. (3) One-week NB case, units 20, mean 15, k 0.25 (r = 225/14.0625 = 16), price 10, salvage 3, elasticity -0.5 (hold): E[min(D,20)] = 14.3846, value 160.6925; tool expectedUnits 14.3843, value 160.6902. (4) Elasticity fit on sampleText() with ref 48, by Frisch-Waugh residualisation on [1, t]: raw slope -2.24299, se 0.22501, residual sd 0.08669; normal-normal shrinkage to prior N(-2, 1): posterior -2.23128, sd 0.21952, 80% band -2.5126 to -1.9499, data weight 0.9518; tool identical to 5 decimals. Sample generator's true base at week 16 is 58 x 0.96^16 = 30.18/wk; tool baseWeekly 31.00. Departures found by probe (probe.mjs): the demand level is exp(intercept) of a log fit with no retransformation and zero weeks dropped, so for low-volume SKUs it is biased low (300 simulated Poisson histories, true 4/wk, elasticity -2: mean baseWeekly 3.678, 8% low; at 60/wk 59.51, under 1%); with 1,001 units the lot rounding models 1,002 and reports sell-through 100.1% and expected leftover -1.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked end to end: date/price/units paste with header detection, week bucketing, decimal-comma files (works); log-log fit with trend control and shrinkage (works, reproduced); refusal when < 8 weeks or price moved < 5% (tests pass); stochastic DP over week, stock, price level with markdown-only moves, floor, max discount and relabel cost (works, reproduced); four baseline rules evaluated by the same recursion (works, hold rule reproduced in closed form); behind/ahead table (works); 4,000-run simulation (mean revenue 15,743.5 vs DP 15,782.2 on the example, consistent); robustness table at the 80% band (works); CSV download (markdownCsv); lots above 1,000 units (works, with the >100% rounding artefact). No TODOs or stubs; the four related-tool links exist as ventures.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject dir: 48 pass, 0 fail (2.8 s); README's `node --test` also 48/48. Tests include a one-week closed form, DP vs Monte Carlo of its own policy, planted-elasticity recovery, monotonicity and floor checks. Six mutants via quality_mutate.py: dropping the stock-out tail revenue in the Bellman update (calc.mjs:321) caught; SE floor 0.15 -> 0.05 (209) survived; Z80 1.2816 -> 1.6449 (15) survived; behind-schedule multiplier 1.25 -> 1.05 (435) survived; demand decay exponent t -> t+1, shifting every week's demand one week of fade (293) survived; decay clamp 0.7 -> 0.5 (228) survived. 1 of 6 caught: the Bellman core is guarded, the parameters that feed it are not.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (521 lines), index.html inline script, usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Pure ES module, one engine for page and tests, Lanczos lgamma, careful date parsing (30 February refused), decimal-comma detection, CSV parsing with quotes. Defects: an unquoted '1,200' in a comma CSV splits into extra columns and the row is read as 1 unit with no warning (calc.mjs:123-124); the 'fit was taken around your last price' note can never fire because fitElasticity is always called with refPrice = the entered price (index.html:192, dead code); lot rounding can model more units than entered (calc.mjs:275-276).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'log-log regression with a time-trend control, shrunk toward a typical retail value' (calc.mjs:185-236, reproduced); 'stochastic dynamic program over weeks, stock and price level' (solve, reproduced); 'simple rules ... evaluated exactly by the same recursion' (calc.mjs:449-453, hold rule reproduced in closed form); 'robustness ... 80% range' (Z80, sensitivity); 'nothing uploaded, no analytics vendors' (usage.mjs localStorage only, DNT/GPC honoured, opt-out; page.test.mjs checks no network); 'Unverified against a published retailer dataset' and 'Not modelled' list disclosed on README and page; disclaimer on README, page header and footer; llms.txt points at the GitHub Pages host but the deploy rewrites it (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin). Gaps: when the elasticity is typed in, the robustness rows use a fixed +-0.6 band (index.html:191) while the page says '80% interval on elasticity'; FAQ 'a 10% price cut sells about 20% more' is a linear approximation of 0.9^-2 = +23.5%.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a boutique owner with 400 units, 10 weeks, $48 price, $8 salvage loads the example and gets 10% off weeks 1-4, 20% weeks 5-9, 30% week 10, 99.0% sell-through, a $443.87 gain over the best simple rule and a Monday behind/ahead table. Usable for one SKU or price group. A merchandise planner would miss markdown dollars and markdown % of sales, gross margin % after markdown and weeks of supply, and cannot plan a class or many SKUs at once. Portfolio fit: verticals.json lists it as the front door for seller-books, but index.html:153 links only to four other free tools; there is no link or CTA to the paid product.
evidence.domain: Compared against the standard clearance-pricing formulation (finite-horizon markdown DP with salvage, e.g. Gallego and van Ryzin 1994; Smith and Achabal 1998; Levy and Weitz retail math for sell-through and markdown %). Method matches: markdown-only price ladder, salvage terminal value, cost treated as sunk, stochastic demand, log-log constant elasticity with a trend control, shrinkage to a prior with an SE floor, exact baseline evaluation. Departures: (1) no lognormal/count retransformation of the intercept and zero weeks dropped, so low-volume demand is under-read about 8% at 4/wk, which pushes the plan to cut earlier; (2) the log-residual sd is used as the NB dispersion k while the residual already contains Poisson noise, so variance is double-counted at low volume (index.html:190); (3) constant elasticity over a 60-70% discount range and no strategic waiting (disclosed); (4) none of the planner KPIs above.
evidence.summary: The markdown DP and elasticity fit reproduce exactly against independent code, and the claims are honest; parameter plumbing is untested (5 of 6 mutants survived), low-volume demand is biased low, and the page does not lead to the paid product it fronts.

mutations.change: Q[j][I] = prices[j] * (sold + I * tail) -> Q[j][I] = prices[j] * (sold)

defects.what: Parameter plumbing around the DP is untested: 5 of 6 seeded mutants survived, including shifting every week's demand by one week of fade (decay^t -> decay^(t+1)), the SE floor, the 80% z value, the behind/ahead multiplier and the decay clamp.

Weekly demand level is exp(intercept) of a log-units fit with no retransformation (smearing or Poisson/NB GLM) and zero-sale weeks dropped, so low-volume demand is read low: true 4/wk gives mean baseWeekly 3.678 (8% low) over 300 simulated histories; the plan then marks down earlier than needed.
Lot rounding (I0 = round(units/lot)) can model more units than entered: 1,001 units -> 1,002 modelled, sell-through 100.1% and expected leftover -1.
An unquoted thousands separator in a comma CSV ('2026-01-12,12.5,1,200') splits into an extra column and the row is read as 1 unit with no warning.
With a typed elasticity the robustness table uses a fixed +-0.6 band, while the page says the plan is re-evaluated at the ends of the 80% interval.
Dead notice: fitElasticity is always given refPrice = the entered price, so 'fit.refPrice !== price' is never true and the note never shows.
Log-residual sd is used as the NB over-dispersion k although it already includes Poisson noise, so at low volume the demand variance is double-counted (wider simulated range, slightly deeper plan).
No planner KPIs: markdown dollars, markdown % of sales, gross margin % after markdown and weeks of supply are not reported, and only one SKU or price group can be planned at a time.
Mapped as the front door for seller-books (portfolio/monetization/verticals.json:1863) but the page has no link or CTA to it; related links go only to free tools.

verdict: The core is right: an independent Python DP, a closed-form hold-price case, a one-week negative-binomial case and a hand OLS-plus-shrinkage all match the tool to within 0.002%, and the README and page disclose method, limits and what is not modelled. It misses the bar on verification: 48 tests pass but 5 of 6 seeded mutants in the parameters feeding the DP survived, including a one-week shift of demand decay. A merchandise planner would also notice that low-volume demand is read about 8% low (no retransformation), that markdown dollars, margin after markdown and weeks of supply are missing, and that the page does not lead to seller-books, the paid product it fronts.
